Special counsel Jack Smith was on Capitol Hill Tuesday, appearing before the Senate
Judiciary Committee, where he defended his prosecutions of Donald Trump and pushed back

My service has spanned both Republican and Democratic administrations.
I am not a politician, and I have no partisan loyalty.
My career has been dedicated to serving our country by upholding the rule of law and the

Smith said he stands by his decision to charge Trump.
Republicans on the panel claimed his investigative tactics were not ethical.
President Trump has released what the White House says is a voluntary accord with major
tech companies on artificial intelligence, saying they've agreed to self-police AI development.
Trump unveiled a one-page document on social media after meeting with tech executives for
a Tuesday lunch at the White House.
The agreement comes amid alarm bells sounded by AI executives who have called on the government
to establish guardrails.
A former Cornell University student's lawsuit alleging she was raped by seven male students
in 2024 is renewing questions about how colleges deal with sexual assault, NPR's Alisson Edwardy
reports.
Title IX prohibits discrimination in schools based on sex.
Under that law, the school's job is to make sure all students have a safe campus environment,
equal access to an education.
In the case of Cornell University, when the district attorney did not move forward with
the criminal investigation back in 2024, the campus Title IX process got underway.
In a statement, Cornell said its investigation took several months and led to expulsions
and suspensions.
The fraternity chapter was closed in 2024.
Title IX has a lower burden of proof than a criminal case.
But in recent years, there have been big changes.
The Trump administration raised the burden of proof and also now requires schools to
conduct "live hearings with cross-examination."
Alisson Edwardy, NPR News.
Making a baby using gene-edited human embryos is effectively illegal in the United States,
but at least two startups are hoping to change that.
NPR's Rob Stein has more.
Origin Genomics in New York City and Preventive Bio in San Francisco are trying to produce
enough evidence to convince regulators that it would be safe to use modified embryos for
reproduction.
The companies say gene-editing embryos could help millions of babies from being born with
rare but devastating genetic disorders.
Critics, however, warn it may never be safe and worry that allowing gene-editing of human
embryos for any reason could open the door to someone trying to go further and create
designer babies.
Rob Stein, NPR News.
And from Washington, you're listening to NPR News.
In Austin, Texas, the Venezuelan man who was shot in the back by immigration enforcement
agents more than a week ago is facing assault charges.
Federal prosecutors announced a charge Tuesday alleging that 28-year-old Wilbur Rafael Garces-Perez
has tried to escape ICE officers who pulled him over after a judge issued a final order
of removal.
If convicted, Garces-Perez faces up to 20 years in prison.
The Education Department extending the enrollment period for student loan borrowers to lower
their interest rates, and Pierre Sequoia Carillo has more.
Nearly two million federal student loan borrowers have already enrolled in auto pay and reduced
their interest rate for the next two years.
The initiative, announced by the Department of Education this summer, aims to get more
borrowers back to regular repayment after the COVID-19 payment freeze.
The department said borrower participation in auto pay dropped from 83 percent in 2019
to just 40 percent in 2025.
Borrowers now have until the end of the calendar year, December 31, to enroll in auto pay.
Those already enrolled in the program do not need to take any action to receive the benefit.
Sequoia Carillo, NPR News.
The National Hurricane Center in Miami expects tropical storm Rachel to strengthen into a
hurricane soon.
Rachel is moving parallel to Mexico's southwestern coast, and forecasters expect the storm to

Meanwhile, the remnants of Hurricane Polo moving into the southwestern U.S., compounding
